Both the civil appeals by leave are directed against the judgment and order dated 14.12.2009 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos.2332 and 2333 of 2007 discharging the Rules. 4. Facts, relevant for disposal of the civil appeals, are that the petitioner herein as pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous Case No.25 of 2001 on 16.04.2001 under section 96(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet, for pre-emption of 1.67 acres of land appertaining to khatian no.530 and 167 respectively as co-sharer by inheritance stating, interalia, that the case land belonged to one Arjan Ullah who died leaving Abdul Motlib, Abul Hashem and Abdul Kader as successive heirs who subsequently sold out 53 decimals of land from plot no.1311 by registered sale deed dated 10.03.1964 to one Ishaque Mia.; Abdul. Motlib, Abul Hasheni sold out 30 decimals of land from plot no.1321 to the said Ishaque Mia by another registered sale deed dated 22.03.1963; Said Abdul Motlib also sold out another 15 decimals of sale deed dated 16.05.1963; Thus, Ishaque Mia became the owner of 53 decimals of land in plot no.1311 and 45 decimals in plot no.1321 who subsequently transferred the same to Mossammat Khairunnessa, step mother of the petitioner, by registered sale deed dated 27.06.1970 and thus, Mossammat Khairunnessa became the co-sharer in the respective khatians; Abdul Motlib and Abdul Kader died leaving pre-emptee-opposite-party nos.6-11 and 12-15 as the successive heirs; Mossammat Khairunnessa also claimed to have purchased 30 decimals of land from one Tayaibullah by registered sale deed dated 28.11.1964; She claimed to have purchased other properties in the said vicinity; Mossammat Khairunnessa died leaving one son, one daughter, husband Haji Jahir Box and pre-emptee nos.36-44; Said Haji Jahir Box died leaving wife preemptee no.20, 7 (seven) sons Md. Azad Box, Md. Afroz Box, pre-emptor no. l and pre-emptee opposite party nos.36-38, 6 daughters pre-emptee opposite party nos.39-44 and 2 daughters of a deceaseds daughter pre-emptee opposite nos.45 and 46; Pre-emptee opposite party nos.36-44 transferred their shares in plot no.1311 and 1321 to Azad Box and others and pre-emptee opposite no.31 by registered sale deed dated 0107.1989; The pre-emptor became the co-sharers in the case land by inheritance and also by purchase; The pre-emptor mutated his name in Mutation Case No.209 of 1 994/9 5; Cause of action arose in the middle of March 2001, when the pre-emptee opposite party no.2 disclosed that he and pre-emptee opposite party no.1 had purchased the case land from pre-emptee opposite party nos. -17; Having came to know about the same, the pre-emptor procured the certified copy of the sale deed dated 12.03.2001 wherefrom he had the definite knowledge that the pre-emptee opposite party nos.3-17 transferred the case land to pre-emptee opposite party nos.1 and 2 at a consideration of Tk.1,00,000/-; No notice was served upon the pre-emptor under section 89 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act; The case land is necessary to the pre-emptor for convenient and effective enjoyment of his existing land; if he knew about the said transfer, he would have purchased the same; Pre-emptee opposite party nos.1 and 2 are strangers to the case holding; The pre-emptor has made statutory deposit with the application for pre-emption. 

 6. During pendency of the trial, pre-emptor-petitioner filed an application on 19.08.2003 to implead the persons named in the application as opposite party nos.54-57 which was allowed by the trial court vide order dated 19.05.2003. Thereafter, on 07.07.2003 the opposite party nos.54-57 made an application before the trial court under section 96(4) of the SAT Act for treating them as co-petitioners contending inter-alia, that the opposite party nos.54-57 i.e. the co-petitioners are the heirs of the original owner Arjan Ullah as such they are the co-sharers by inheritance in the case holding appertaining to Khatian Nos.530 and 167; The property left by the original owner remains unpartitioned and all the properties are ejmali property; For convenient use and enjoyment of the lands the case holding is necessary to the co-petitioners; The pre-emptor intentionally did not implead them as party to the pre-emption case and the transfer of the case land was beyond the knowledge of the co-petitioners; The co-petitioners are ready to abide by the decision of the court under section 96(6) of the SAT Act to deposit the consideration money. 

 35. Facts leading to filing of this civil appeals, in short, are that the petitioner as preemptor filed Miscellaneous Case No.25 of 2001 on 16.4.2001 under section 96(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in short, SAT Act), 1950 before the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Syihet for pre-emption of 1.67 acres of land appertaining to Khatian Nos.530 and 167 respectively as co-sharer by inheritance stating, inter alias that the case land originally belonged to one Arjan Ullah, who died leaving behind Abdul Motlib, Abdul Hashem and Abdul Kadir as heirs who subsequently sold out 53 decimals of land of plot No.1311 by executing registered sale deed dated 10.03.1964 to one Ishaquc Mia. Abdul Motlib and Abdul Hashem sold out 30 decimals of land of plot No.1321 to said lshaque Mia vide registered sale deed dated 22.03.1963. That Abdul Motlib also sold out another 15 decimals of land of plot No.1321 to ishaquc Mia vide registered sale deed dated 16.05.1.963. Accordingly, Ishaque Mia became the owner of 53 decimals of land of plot No.1311 and 45 decimals of land of plot No.1321. Subsequently, he transferred the same to one Mosammat Khairunnessa, the step mother of the petitioner vide sale deed dated 27.6.1970. As such, Mosammat Khairunnessa became the co-sharer in the respective khatians. The .Abdul Motlib and Abdul Kader died leaving behind pre-emptee Nos. 6-11, 12-16 as heirs. Mosammat Khairunnessa also claimed to have purchased 30 decimals of land from one Tayaibullah vide registered sale deed dated 2811.1964 and she claimed to have purchased other proper-ties in the said vicinity. While Mosammat Khairunnessa was enjoying 83 decimals of land of plot No.111, and 45 decimals of land of plot No.1321, she died leaving behind a son, a daughter, her husband Hazi Zahir Bakth and the pre-emptee Nos.36-44. That Hazi Zahir Bakth died leaving behind one wife, the pre-emptee No. 20, seven sons, Md Azad Bakth, Md. Afna Bakth, the pre-emptor, pre-ernptee Nos. 36-38, six daughters, pre-emptce Nos. 39-44 and 2 daughters of a deceased daughter pre-emptee Nos.45-46. That pre-emptee Nos.36-44 transferred their respective shares of plot Nos.1311 and 1321 to Azad Bakth and others, including the pre-emptor and premptee No.31, vide registered sale deed dated 03.07.1989. Hence, the pre-emptors became the co-sharers in the case land by inheritance and also by purchase. The pre-emptors mutated their names vide Mutation Case No.209 of 1994-95. The cause of action arose in the middle part of March, 2001 when the pre-emptee No.2 disclosed in the locality that the pre-emptee No.1 and he purchased the case land from pre-emptee Nos.3-17. Having come to know about the alleged transfer, the preemptors obtained the certified copy of the sale deed dated 12.03.2001 wherefrom it was disclosed that the pre-emptee Nos.3-17 transferred the case land to pre-emptee Nos.1-2 for consideration of taka one lac. It has been alleged that, no notice was served upon the pre-emptors under section 89 of the SAT Act and that the case land was necessary to the pre-emptors and that had they known about the said transfer, they would have purchased the same. That the pre-emptors had deposited the requisite amount of money for the purpose of pre-emption and filed the suit.
